title: Reducing quantum resources for ADAPT-VQE via plateau-operator elimination and correlated mean-field downfolding
authors: Phuoc Minh Vo, Thai Cong Ngoc Vu, Thien Ngoc Tran, Hoang Thanh Nguyen, Lan Nguyen Tran
abstract: Adaptive Derivative-Assembled Problem-Tailored variational quantum eigensolvers (ADAPT-VQE) represent one of the most promising approaches for quantum chemistry on near-term quantum devices. However, their optimization is slow and may stall due to vanishing parameters and redundant operators in the ansatz. In this work, we propose a simple strategy of operator elimination that removes non-contributing operators from the pool once they are detected, enabling the optimization to continue progressing toward convergence. We examine two variants, with and without pool restoration after elimination, and find that the former converges more smoothly and faster than the latter and the standard ADAPT-VQE. To capture dynamical correlations between the active space and its environment, we combine ADAPT-VQE with our recently developed downfolding approach, the one-body downfolding framework (OBDF). In OBDF, the bare molecular Hamiltonian in the active space is replaced by a correlated effective Hamiltonian that incorporates dynamical correlation effects outside the active space. We benchmark our implementation on a linear \ce{H_6} chain, an \ce{H_6} lattice, an \ce{H_6} ring, and the \ce{N_2} molecule using the OpenFermion simulator. Our results show that operator elimination significantly reduces circuit depth and iteration count, and that OBDF-ADAPT-VQE yields energies closer to the full configuration interaction (FCI) reference than the standard approach within the same active space.
summary: The paper presents an advanced hybrid quantum algorithm combining operator elimination with a one-body downfolding framework (OBDF) to enhance ADAPT-VQE for electronic structure calculations. By pruning redundant operators and incorporating external correlation effects, the method achieves faster convergence and higher accuracy compared to standard approaches on molecular models like H6 and N2.
main_problem: The primary goal is to reduce quantum resources and improve convergence stability for ADAPT-VQE, a method used for electronic structure calculations on near-term quantum devices.
main_result: Operator elimination significantly reduces circuit depth and iteration count, while combining this technique with the one-body downfolding framework (OBDF) yields energies closer to the FCI reference than standard methods.
method: The work introduces plateau-operator elimination into ADAPT-VQE to prune redundant operators during ansatz construction. This is combined with OBDF, which replaces the bare Hamiltonian in the active space with a correlated effective Hamiltonian incorporating external correlation effects.
model_or_system: The methodology is applied to quantum chemistry problems, benchmarked on molecular systems including linear H6 chains, H6 lattices, H6 rings, and the N2 molecule. The underlying physics involves solving electronic structure Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Energy expectation value (compared to FCI), CNOT gate counts (circuit depth), and convergence rate of energy gradients.
important_parameters: The elimination threshold ($\delta$) for vanishing parameters, the active space definition, and the correlation effects captured by OBDF.
main_assumptions: Permanent operator elimination is preferred over pool restoration due to observed instabilities; the assumption is that eliminating non-contributing operators reduces overhead without sacrificing accuracy.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate how plateau-operator elimination stabilizes convergence (e.g., H6 chain), shows significant reduction in CNOT gate counts across various systems, and compares energy surfaces (PES) of H6/N2 using different levels of theory including OBDF-ADAPT-VQE.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the limitations of standard ADAPT-VQE. It then details the operator elimination strategy, showing its benefits in convergence speed and resource reduction. Finally, it integrates this with the OBDF framework to systematically improve accuracy by incorporating external correlation effects, benchmarking on multiple molecular systems.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the practical limitations of applying quantum algorithms (like VQE) to complex many-body Hamiltonians, providing concrete algorithmic improvements for resource efficiency and systematic error reduction in correlated electron simulations.
